source_refs.note: Book p. 104-105: 6.7 Geometric Series, e-mail forwarding tree (original SVG), S_n = a1(1 - r^n)/(1 - r) derived by subtracting rS_n, Note r = 1, Example 18

blocks.text: Ab tak humne G.P. ki terms nikaalna seekha. Lekin aksar sawal yeh hota hai ke itni saari terms ka jama (sum) kitna hai? Masalan bank mein har saal barhne wali raqam ka kul, ya kisi khabar ka phailna. Is hisse mein hum G.P. ki terms ko jama karne ka shortcut formula banayenge, aur kitab ki ek pyari si misaal se shuru karenge.

Kitab ki misaal: maan lijiye aap Monday ko ek Islamic quote teen doston ko e-mail karte hain. Har dost Tuesday ko use apne teen doston ko bhejta hai. Tuesday ko jis ko bhi quote mila, woh Wednesday ko teen aur logon ko bhejta hai, aur yeh silsila aise hi chalta rehta hai.

blocks.alt: E-Mail window mein forwarding ka tree. Ooper ek shakhs Monday ko quote 3 logon ko bhejta hai; un mein se har ek Tuesday ko 3 logon ko bhejta hai (9 log); un mein se har ek Wednesday ko 3 logon ko bhejta hai (27 log). Baayein taraf har din ke liye lifafe (envelope) ka nishan aur dotted line hai.
blocks.caption: Figure: Monday, Tuesday aur Wednesday ka e-mail forwarding tree, har shakhs quote teen doston ko bhejta hai (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Ghor kijiye ke har din quote parhne walon ki tadaad pichle din ki teen guna hai. Sunday tak, aap ko mila kar, quote parhne walon ki kul tadaad \(1 + 3 + 9 + 27 + 81 + 243 + 729 + 2187\), yani \(3280\) hai. Numbers \(1, 3, 9, 27, 81, 243, 729\) aur \(2187\) ek geometric sequence banate hain jis mein \(a_1 = 1\) aur \(r = 3\). In numbers ke jama ki shakal, \(1 + 3 + 9 + 27 + 81 + 243 + 729 + 2187\), ko geometric series kehte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Sequence aur series mein farq zaroor samajh lein: sequence sirf list hai, \(1, 3, 9, 27, \ldots\) (commas ke saath). Series us list ka jama hai, \(1 + 3 + 9 + 27 + \cdots\) (plus ke saath). Neeche table dekhiye ke har term teen guna hone se kul kitni tezi se barhta hai: sirf ek hafte mein 3280 log!

blocks.caption: Har din quote parhne wale log

blocks.title: Kyun
blocks.text: Yeh misaal kyun di gayi? Taa ke aap mehsoos karein ke G.P. ki terms ko ek ek kar ke jama karna kitna lamba kaam hai. 8 terms to theek, lekin agar 30 din ka hisaab chahiye ho to? Is liye humein ek formula chahiye jo seedha jawab de de.

Geometric progression ka jama yun likha ja sakta hai:
\[S_n = \dfrac{a_1(1 - r^{n})}{1 - r},\ r \ne 1\]

Ab dekhte hain yeh formula aaya kahan se. Kisi bhi geometric series ka formula banane ke liye yeh likhiye:
\[S_n = a_1 + a_1r + a_1r^{2} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + a_1r^{n-3} + a_1r^{n-2}\]
\[\quad + a_1r^{n-1} \quad \text{(i)}\]
\[rS_n = a_1r + a_1r^{2} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + a_1r^{n-3} + a_1r^{n-2}\]
\[\quad + a_1r^{n-1} + a_1r^{n} \quad \text{(ii)}\]

blocks.title: Kyun
blocks.text: (ii) kahan se aayi? (i) ke dono taraf \(r\) se zarb kiya. Har term ki power ek barh gayi: \(a_1\) ban gaya \(a_1r\), \(a_1r\) ban gaya \(a_1r^{2}\), aur aakhri term \(a_1r^{n-1}\) ban gayi \(a_1r^{n}\). Hum ne (ii) ki terms ko ek jagah aage khiska kar likha hai taa ke same power wali terms ek doosre ke neeche aa jayein.

Ab (ii) ko (i) mein se tafreeq (subtract) karein. Beech ki saari terms \(a_1r, a_1r^{2}, \ldots, a_1r^{n-1}\) dono mein hain, is liye cut ho jati hain; sirf (i) ki pehli term aur (ii) ki aakhri term bachti hai:
\[S_n - rS_n = a_1 - a_1r^{n}\]
\[S_n(1 - r) = a_1(1 - r^{n})\]
\[S_n = \dfrac{a_1(1 - r^{n})}{1 - r},\ r \ne 1\]

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab is line ko \(S_n - rS_n = a_1 - ar^{n}\) chhaapti hai, yani \(a_1\) ki jagah sirf \(a\). Sahi line \(S_n - rS_n = a_1 - a_1r^{n}\) hai, kyun ke (ii) ki aakhri term \(a_1r^{n}\) hai. Kitab ki agli line \(S_n(1 - r) = a_1(1 - r^{n})\) phir se \(a_1\) use karti hai, is liye aakhri formula bilkul sahi hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(r \ne 1\) ki shart kyun? Kyun ke aakhri qadam mein hum \(1 - r\) se divide karte hain, aur \(r = 1\) par \(1 - r = 0\) ho jata hai; zero se divide karna mumkin nahin. Lekin \(r = 1\) wali series to bohat aasan hai: har term \(a_1\) hi hai (jaise \(5 + 5 + 5 + 5\)), to \(n\) terms ka jama \(na_1\). Yahi note box keh raha hai.
Ek aur kaam ki baat: upar neeche dono ko \(-1\) se zarb karein to wahi formula yun ban jata hai: \(S_n = \frac{a_1(r^{n} - 1)}{r - 1}\). Jab \(r > 1\) ho (jaise 3), to yeh shakal behtar hai kyun ke dono brackets positive rehti hain aur minus signs ki ulajhan nahin hoti.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Formula ki tasdeeq e-mail wali series se: \(a_1 = 1\), \(r = 3\), \(n = 8\) (aap se Sunday tak 8 terms).
\[S_8 = \dfrac{1(3^{8} - 1)}{3 - 1} = \dfrac{6561 - 1}{2}\]
\[S_8 = 3280\]
Bilkul wahi jawab jo ek ek kar ke jama karne se aaya tha, magar ek line mein!
Ab kitab ki misaal dekhte hain jis mein \(a_1\) aur \(r\) chhupe hue hain; pehle unhein dhoondna hoga.

blocks.title: Example 18
blocks.problem: Find the sum of \(n\) terms of the geometric series if \(a_n = (-3)\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^{n}\).
steps:
Given: geometric series ki general term \(a_n = (-3)\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^{n}\).
To find: \(S_n\), yani pehli \(n\) terms ka jama.
Method: sab se pehle sochte hain ke sum ka formula kya maangta hai: \(a_1\) (pehli term) aur \(r\) (common ratio). Sawal mein yeh seedhe nahin diye, sirf \(a_n\) diya hai. Is liye plan yeh hai: \(a_n\) ko standard shakal \(a_1r^{n-1}\) mein likhein, wahan se \(a_1\) aur \(r\) parh lein, phir \(S_n = \frac{a_1(1 - r^{n})}{1 - r}\) lagayein.

Step 1: \(a_n\) ko power \(n - 1\) wali shakal mein likhein
\[(-3)\left(\tfrac{2}{5}\right)^{n} = -3\left(\tfrac{2}{5}\right)\left(\tfrac{2}{5}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[= \left(-\tfrac{6}{5}\right)\left(\tfrac{2}{5}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[a_n = \left(-\tfrac{6}{5}\right)\left(\tfrac{2}{5}\right)^{n-1}\]
Kyun: indices ka rule hai \(x^{n} = x \cdot x^{n-1}\) (jaise \(2^{5} = 2 \times 2^{4}\)). Ek \(\frac{2}{5}\) bahar nikaalne se power \(n - 1\) ho jati hai jo standard form mein hoti hai, aur bahar wala \(\frac{2}{5}\) \(-3\) se zarb ho kar \(-\frac{6}{5}\) ban jata hai.

Step 2: \(a_1\) aur \(r\) pehchaanein
\(\left(-\frac{6}{5}\right)\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^{n-1}\) ko \(a_1r^{n-1}\) se milaayein:
\[a_1 = -\tfrac{6}{5},\quad r = \tfrac{2}{5}\]
Kyun: \(a_1r^{n-1}\) mein aage wala number pehli term hai aur power ka base common ratio hai.
Dhyan dein: chhoti si tasdeeq kar lein. Diye hue \(a_n\) mein \(n = 1\) rakhein: \((-3)\frac{2}{5} = -\frac{6}{5}\). Haan, pehli term yahi hai, \(-3\) nahin.

Step 3: Sum ka formula lagayein
\[S_n = \dfrac{a_1(1 - r^{n})}{1 - r}\]
\[= \dfrac{-\frac{6}{5}\left[1 - \left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^{n}\right]}{1 - \frac{2}{5}}\]
Kyun: \(r = \frac{2}{5}\) hai jo 1 nahin, is liye formula lag sakta hai. Aur \(r\) 1 se chhota hai, is liye \(1 - r\) wali shakal behtar hai: neeche positive number aata hai aur hisaab saaf rehta hai.

Step 4: Simplify karein
\[1 - \tfrac{2}{5} = \tfrac{3}{5}\]
\[S_n = \left(-\tfrac{6}{5}\right)\left(\tfrac{5}{3}\right)\left[1 - \left(\tfrac{2}{5}\right)^{n}\right]\]
\[S_n = (-2)\left[1 - \left(\tfrac{2}{5}\right)^{n}\right]\]
Kyun: kisi fraction se divide karna us ke ulte (reciprocal) se zarb dene ke barabar hai, is liye \(\frac{3}{5}\) se divide = \(\frac{5}{3}\) se zarb. Phir \(-\frac{6}{5}\times\frac{5}{3}\) mein 5 cut ho jata hai aur \(-\frac{6}{3} = -2\) bachta hai.

Tasdeeq:
Ab dekhte hain ke formula sach mein sahi jama deta hai ya nahin.
\(n = 1\): \(-2\left(1 - \frac{2}{5}\right) = -2 \times \frac{3}{5} = -\frac{6}{5}\), jo pehli term hi hai.
\(n = 2\): seedha jama \(a_1 + a_2 = -\frac{6}{5} + (-3)\frac{4}{25} = -\frac{30}{25} - \frac{12}{25} = -\frac{42}{25}\). Formula se: \(-2\left(1 - \frac{4}{25}\right) = -2 \times \frac{21}{25} = -\frac{42}{25}\). Dono barabar, jawab durust hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Series \(2 + 6 + 18 + \cdots\) ki pehli 5 terms ka jama nikaaliye. Yahan \(a_1 = 2\), \(r = \frac{6}{2} = 3\), \(n = 5\). \(r > 1\) hai, is liye doosri shakal lein:
\[S_5 = \dfrac{2(3^{5} - 1)}{3 - 1} = \dfrac{2 \times 242}{2} = 242\]
Tasdeeq: \(2 + 6 + 18 + 54 + 162 = 242\). Sahi!

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
1. \(1 + \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{4} + \cdots\) ki pehli 5 terms ka jama formula se nikaaliye. (Jawab \(\frac{31}{16}\) aana chahiye.)
2. \(4 + 4 + 4 + \cdots\) (10 terms) ka jama kya hai? Kaunsa formula lagega?
3. Agar \(a_n = 5 \cdot 2^{n}\) ho to \(a_1\) aur \(r\) kya honge?

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. G.P. ki terms ka jama geometric series kehlata hai.
2. \(S_n = \frac{a_1(1 - r^{n})}{1 - r} = \frac{a_1(r^{n} - 1)}{r - 1}\), jab \(r \ne 1\).
3. \(r = 1\) ho to \(S_n = na_1\).
4. Formula ka tareeqa: \(S_n\) likho, \(rS_n\) likho, tafreeq karo; beech ki terms cut.
5. Sirf \(a_n\) diya ho to use \(a_1r^{n-1}\) ki shakal mein likh kar \(a_1\) aur \(r\) nikaalo.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(a_n = (-3)\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^{n}\) dekh kar foran \(a_1 = -3\) likh dena: power \(n\) hai, \(n - 1\) nahin, is liye \(a_1 = -\frac{6}{5}\). Bachne ka tareeqa: hamesha \(n = 1\) rakh kar pehli term check karein.
2. Sum ke formula mein \(r^{n}\) ki jagah \(r^{n-1}\) likh dena: \(r^{n-1}\) general term mein aata hai, sum mein \(r^{n}\).
3. \(r = 1\) par bhi formula laga dena, jis se zero se division ho jata hai.
4. Fraction se divide karte waqt ulta (reciprocal) karna bhool jana.
